newsitem.title: USA: Jury rules in favor of Polaroid in lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Jury rules in favor of Polaroid in lawsuit.

text.p: Polaroid Corp said Tuesday a federal court jury in Boston had cleared the company of allegations that it discriminated on the basis of race in denying disability benefits to and subsequently terminating an employee.

Polaroid said the jury verdict came after a five-day trial presided over by U.S. District Judge Robert Keeton. The trial was ordered as part of a ruling by the First Circuit Court of Appeals last year that overturned a 1995 $400,000 verdict against Polaroid and dismissed certain claims made by the employee, Ollie Lattimore.

Polaroid said Lattimore was terminated in 1989 from a job at the company's camera assembly operation in Norwood, Mass., after failing to return to work following a determination by a third-party physician that he was not entitled to short-term disability benefits.
